action: Wait for the airline's notice if you booked with Caribbean Airlines and treat unexpected messages about your booking with caution.
title: Caribbean Airlines says Amadeus reported unauthorised access to booking data
date_note: Date of Caribbean Airlines' statement, datelined Port of Spain.
exec: A reservations supplier's incident exposed an airline's passenger booking data; supplier incidents can reach customers' data.
plain: Caribbean Airlines says its reservations provider Amadeus reported that an unauthorised party accessed booking and reservation information. The airline says preliminary data suggests no payment card data was accessed.
summary: Caribbean Airlines said on 15 November that its reservations provider, Amadeus IT Group, reported that an unauthorised party exploited a vulnerability to gain access to booking and reservation information. The airline says the breach was limited to passengers' booking or travel data and that preliminary data from Amadeus suggests no payment card data was accessed. It says notifying affected customers is ongoing and that Amadeus has fixed the vulnerability.

validation.note: Two publishers (iNews Guyana carrying the airline's statement, Travelers Today) state the core fact; the airline's own page and Amadeus's statement were not read. No count of affected passengers was given.

review.note: Compared date 15 Nov, Amadeus, exploited vulnerability, preliminary no-payment-card wording, notification ongoing, fixed, no count against the airline statement (iNews Guyana) and Travelers Today
